newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Africa must lure oil exploration -SAfrica minister.
newsitem.headline: Africa must lure oil exploration -SAfrica minister.

text.p: African countries must make it attractive for oil and gas exploration companies to invest, South African Minister of Mineral and Energy Affairs Penuell Maduna said on Wednesday.

"Oil and gas explorers are not here to primarily provide energy to Africa. They are here to economically exploit oil and gas. In short they are here to make profit," Maduna said in his opening address to the Africa Upstream 1996 conference.
But he added that these companies provided a catalyst for Africa's economic growth and African governments should create an environment conducive to an adequate return on investment.

"The companies represented here today as well as other companies are responsible companies. They are not only concerned with bottom-line profits. They do not look upon the oil and gas resources of Africa as mere resources of black gold," Maduna said. Delegates from around the world are attending the three-day conference which will also see the launch of the first African Institute of Petroleum, referred to by Maduna as "a potentially momentous event in the history of Africa's development".
The institute aims to attract investment to Africa and facilitate collaboration between governments on energy policy to achieve some sector policy standardisation.
Maduna urged international private companies to pledge their commitment to the institute.
"A similar commitment on the part of exploration companies would greatly assist us," he said.
"We can begin a serious process of transforming the lives of ordinary people from the Cape to Cairo. Together we can really take Africa upstream in '96 and beyond," he said.
Maduna called on African states to create stable and investor-friendly fiscal and monetary regimes and political environments free from corruption and violence.

Addressing companies represented, like Mobil Corp, Exxon Exploration Co Ltd, Total Exploration Production and British Petroleum, he said: "We cannot expect you to run the risks and hazards in our societies which should be the responsibilities of our governments to eliminate or reduce."

He said Africa's petroleum product markets needed to become more cohesive, over-regulation needed to be reduced and over-subsidised prices eliminated, and governments needed to tackle high distribution and supply costs, as well as the inefficiencies of energy procurement.
Vast resources in Africa remained relatively unknown and investment was needed to reap the benefits of these, he said.
